title: privnet traffic-filter fabric: terraform module for subnet NACLs, SGs, private DNS and controlled egress
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (privnet-traffic-filter) that enforces subnet-level and instance-level network controls for Redwood Private deployments on AWS. The module will provide opinionated defaults plus knobs for customization: security groups (instance-level), NACLs (subnet-level), private DNS forwarding/resolver rules, and a configurable egress enforcement pattern (egress-proxy vs. route-based NAT vs. Network Firewall). It must include upgrade/migration helpers, automated health checks, and CI checks to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes inputs for SG rules, NACL rule sets, private DNS resolver rules and an egress_mode variable (proxy | nat | firewall)
Module creates outputs for resource ids (sg_id, nacl_id, route_table_ids, resolver_rule_id) and a canonical set of tags matching Redwood standards
Upgrade path documented for changing NACL order or converting subnets between NAT and proxy patterns without downtime

Automated Terratest suite validates key scenarios: (a) default deploy, (b) deny-by-default egress, (c) canary with proxy and fallback to NAT, (d) private DNS resolution for service.internal -> VPC resolver
CI includes policy checks: tfsec / checkov pass and OPA policy preventing wide 0.0.0.0/0 ingress on SGs
Operational health checks emit metrics to CloudWatch/Prometheus (egress_allowed_count, dns_resolution_failures, nacl_rejected_packets) and a Console dashboard template is provided
Module supports state import scripts and a sample migration runbook for customers moving from permissive egress to allowlist egress
Security review completed and audit-logging of changes is enabled (CloudTrail logs + KMS-encrypted S3 for plan artifacts)
technical_notes: Root module will compose submodules: sg/, nacl/, dns_resolver/, egress_gateway/ to keep resource boundaries clear

Egress patterns: proxy uses managed envoy ASG + route table to forward via proxy ENIs; nat uses per-AZ NAT Gateway or NAT Gateway Autoscaling; firewall uses AWS Network Firewall stateful rules with Suricata-like rule translations
NACLs are stateless and ordering matters; we will generate intent-based rule numbers and provide migration helpers that create replacement NACLs then swap associations to avoid order drift
Private DNS: implement Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound rules and resolver rule associations for shared VPCs; include resolver endpoint lifecycle with idempotent creation
Terraform constraints: require >= 1.5, AWS provider pinned to 5.x+; enforce provider aliasing for multi-account deployments
State migration helpers: scripted 'terraform import' helpers and small Go utility for diffing current rules vs desired with safe-change prompts
Instrumentation: add CloudWatch metrics and log groups; export metrics via prom-exporter on a small observability agent deployed into privnet management plane
Testing: Terratest for infra-level tests and a lighter local harness with localstack for fast CI; include negative tests for deny rules and DNS poisoning simulations
RBAC: module creates IAM role assumptions only for control-plane agents; no user-managed keys embedded. KMS keys must be passed in as inputs for encryption of plan artifacts
decisions: Prefer dual-layer defense: SGs for instance-level intent, NACLs for coarse subnet boundaries. Both are implemented; SGs are primary for inbound intent, NACLs are used for egress default-deny enforcement.

Provide three egress modes but default to 'proxy' for audited, per-request allowlisting and easier observability. 'nat' kept for low-latency data-plane, 'firewall' for customers with IDS/IPS requirements.
Avoid embedding vendor-specific metadata in tags beyond required keys; allow a policy hook for organizations to inject additional tagging via input variable
Do not automatically delete old NACLs during migration — instead orphan and mark for manual cleanup to avoid accidental traffic disruption
